pieces.text: Test results, scanned cards and signed forms.

pieces.text: Ask the camp or school what they need, and follow their instructions.

alt: A table of the order camp and school forms usually ask in, from who and who to call through insurance, health and vaccines, with a note to ask the camp what it needs.
caption: Many forms follow this order, so your page can too.

items: What is taken now, dose, how often
Who to call: you, a second person
What to do in an emergency

pieces.text: Insurance member ID and the full vaccine record.

alt: A sitter sheet checklist covering allergies, what is taken now, who to call, emergency steps and bedtime notes, beside a note on what to leave off.
caption: What goes on a one-page sheet for a sitter or grandparent.

steps.what: List what is taken now, note symptoms
Note what was said, while fresh

alt: A timeline for a doctor visit: write questions, list what is taken and note symptoms the day before, bring the insurance card, then note what was said afterward.
caption: A short paperwork list for the day before a doctor visit.

pieces.title: Amina, 8: tomorrow's visit
items: Is the new brand the same drug?
Can you sign the camp form?

pieces.text: Tick each line as it is answered. Ask what's left before you go.

alt: A checklist of four short questions for a child's doctor visit, the most important first, beside a note about ticking each one off in the room.
caption: Example: four questions, one line each, the important one first.

pieces.text: Allergy: penicillin (rash). Checked against the bottles 09/20/2026.

alt: A sample medication list with four medicines and how often each is taken, beside a note with an allergy and the date the list was checked against the bottles.
caption: Example: copied from the labels, with the date it was last checked.

pieces.text: Write what you saw, not what you think it is.

alt: A sample symptom log with three dated lines showing what happened and how bad it was, beside a note to write what you saw, not what you think it is.
caption: Example: one dated line each time, what you saw and how bad.

pieces.text: A printed sheet is only what you typed, on the day you typed it.

alt: A sample emergency sheet for a child with the emergency number, an allergy, a first contact, the doctor and the poison help line, beside a note that it is not a medical ID.
caption: Example: the lines someone needs first, with allergies near the top.

pieces.text: Photo ID, insurance card, and the bottles.

alt: A one-page example intake summary for a first doctor visit with allergies, medicines, conditions, family history and symptoms, beside a note about ID, insurance card and bottles.
caption: An example first-visit page, with made-up details.

pieces.text: Does this person need this fact to do what I'm asking?

alt: A comparison of what goes on a sitter page (allergy, tonight's medicine, who to call) and what stays with the parent (family history, insurance ID, old symptoms).
caption: An example of one child's page for a sitter, and what stays home.

pieces.text: One person per page. Print one at a time.

alt: A table comparing a child's and a parent's page under the same headings of allergies, medicines and doctors, beside a note: one person per page, print one at a time.
caption: An example of the same headings for a child and a parent.
